simple.meaning: פִּיחַ (pîyach) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a powder (as easily puffed away), i.e. ashes or dust.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Exodus 9:8. The surrounding context includes kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פִּיחַ (H6368) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

structuredEvidence.definition: a powder (as easily puffed away), i.e. ashes or dust

firstOccurrence.englishText: Yahweh said to Moses and to Aaron, “Take handfuls of ashes of the furnace, and let Moses sprinkle it toward the sky in the sight of Pharaoh.

timeline.evidenceText: Yahweh said to Moses and to Aaron, “Take handfuls of ashes of the furnace, and let Moses sprinkle it toward the sky in the sight of Pharaoh.
They took ashes of the furnace, and stood before Pharaoh; and Moses sprinkled it up toward the sky; and it became boils and blisters breaking on man and on animal.
